epic.title: EPIC-25: Multi-Language Support (French, British English, American English, Spanish)
epic.functionalNeed:
GEO is currently English only. Every screen, label, button, tooltip, empty state, wizard step, settings page, and notification is shown in English regardless of who is using it. This blocks adoption for users who do not work in English and leaves GEO out of step with the rest of the Onclusive platform, which already runs in several languages. A French or Spanish user has no way to work in their own language, and a user who reads English as a second language has to translate the interface in their head before they can act on what the analysis is telling them.
This EPIC makes the GEO interface available in four languages: French, British English, American English, and Spanish. Each user has an active language that drives the entire interface they see. The active language is seeded from the value Auth0 holds for the user, suggested as the default when the user is added to GEO, and can be overridden both at that moment and later by the user in their own settings. Because each Onclusive app handles language independently, the value the user chooses inside GEO stays inside GEO and is not written back to Auth0. Once a language is active, the full interface follows it: navigation, controls, labels, table headers, tooltips, and empty states, plus the analysis wizard, onboarding, the user administration and settings screens, and the transactional emails GEO sends, each delivered in the recipient's own language. Where a given piece of text has not yet been translated into the active language, the interface falls back to English rather than showing blank space or a missing-text marker, so a partially translated screen is always readable.
---
Story ID: TBD
> As an administrator adding a user to GEO, I want the user's language to be suggested from the value Auth0 already holds, so that most users get the right language without anyone having to set it manually.
Acceptance Criteria:
scope: - Interface text: navigation, buttons, labels, table headers, tooltips, and empty states
- Transactional emails, sent in the recipient's language
- Translating the analysis content itself (brand and competitor names, source text, and AI-generated narrative summaries), which follow the language of the markets being analysed
- Writing the GEO-chosen language back to Auth0 or to any other Onclusive app
- Adding languages beyond the four supported ones
- Confirm that translation strings reuse the surrounding platform's existing terminology where equivalent terms already exist, rather than being authored fresh
Translation GEO - source of truth file for PM, R&D, and QA:

stories.title: [25.10] Collapse UI language to a single users.language column (technical refactor)
stories.userStory:
**Epic:** GEO-576 (Multi-Language Support) · **Technical refactor** (architect decision, 2026-06-23). **No functional behavior change.**

## Context
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
**None new — functional behavior is unchanged.** The functional ACs of **GEO-684 / GEO-721 / GEO-801 / GEO-802** remain valid verbatim: admin sets the GEO interface language at creation; the user self-switches in Settings; all four locales (incl. en-GB / es-ES) work; the GEO choice is never propagated to Auth0. This ticket is a pure technical refactor of how that behavior is persisted (1 column instead of 2).


1. **Migration (flyway clean, local-only)** — rewrite `V2.0.1__create_users_table.sql`: `language VARCHAR(10) DEFAULT 'en-US' NOT NULL` (was `'en'`), comment block updated to the GEO-owned full-locale semantics; **delete** `V2.5.9__add_users_ui_language_preference.sql`. Local DB reset / `flyway clean` (no backfill, no data preserved — OS-Team decision). MPD + `database_schema.md` updated in the **same** change (invariant: MPD in sync with migrations at all times).

2. **Entity** — remove `User.uiLanguagePreference` (field + getter/setter); `language` default init → `"en-US"`; javadoc updated.

3. **Read-path** — `AuthMeService.resolveServedLanguage(user)` returns `user.getLanguage()` directly (already a full GEO locale); thin defensive guard → `DEFAULT_GEO_LOCALE` if null/invalid. The `ui_language_preference ?? map(language) ?? en-US` chain is removed.

4. **Self-service write-path** — `AuthMeService.updateOwnUiLanguage(uiLanguage)` validates via `GeoUiLocaleSupport.isValidLocale` (400 otherwise) → `user.setLanguage(uiLanguage)` (verbatim, en-GB/es-ES incl.) → save. Single effective `@Transactional`. **No** Auth0/Middleware call. Self-only (target = principal from JWT).

5. **Provisioning write-path** (`AdminUserService.provision`/`create`) — store the chosen **full GEO locale** directly in `users.language`. For a **NOT_FOUND** Auth0 user, the Middleware/Auth0 seed still **collapses** to the allowlisted short code (`en-GB→en`, etc.) via `GeoUiLocaleSupport.toShortSeed` — now a **transient** transform, not a stored column. For **EXISTS_AUTH0_ONLY**, no Auth0/Middleware push (AC3) — the chosen GEO locale is still stored in `users.language`. `CreateUserRequest.uiLanguagePreference` removed; `language` = full GEO locale.

6. **All seed paths map short→full** — `GeoOidcCallbackHandler` (first-login) and the GUM webhook (`GumEventHandler`) must write the **full GEO locale** (`GeoUiLocaleSupport.servedLocale` mapping) so the column never becomes heterogeneous (it is served verbatim by `/auth/me`).

7. `GeoUiLocaleSupport` — kept as the single backend locale source. Usages shift: `servedLocale` now used at **seed** time (short→full), no longer in the `/auth/me` read-path; `toShortSeed` (Middleware collapse) + `normaliseAuth0ToShort` (wizard preselect read-path) + `emailLocale` (defensive, en-GB→en) unchanged.

8. **Frontend** — no behavior change: `SettingsView` reads `user.language` (now the full locale directly); `resolveSupportedLanguage` / `AUTH0_LANG_MAP` kept (defensive); `ProvisioningWizard` payload = full GEO locale; remove `uiLanguagePreference` from `backoffice/api/types.ts`.

9. **Tests** — rewrite assertions targeting `ui_language_preference` → `users.language` (`AdminUserServiceLanguageTest`, `AuthMeServiceTest`); keep `AuthControllerTest` HTTP contract, `useUpdateUiLanguage.test.ts`, `SettingsView.test.tsx`, `ProvisioningWizard.test`. `mvn verify` + `pnpm check`/`lint:i18n` green.

10. **Docs (source of truth)** — `architecture.md`: replace the _GEO UI language override_ 2-column section with the single-column model and **remove** the documented deviation. MPD + `database_schema.md`: drop `ui_language_preference`, update `language` semantics.

stories.title: [25.7] GEO UI language preference — admin-set at user creation
stories.userStory: As an org administrator creating a GEO user, I want to set the user's **GEO interface language** at creation — editable even when the user already exists in Auth0 — stored **only on the GEO side** without writing back to Auth0, so that the user lands in GEO in the chosen language and the **QA team can exercise all four i18n locales from administration**, without affecting the user's language in the other Onclusive apps.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Given** the user-creation wizard, **When** the language dropdown is shown, **Then** it offers the four languages (American English, British English, French, Spanish) and is **editable in all cases** — including when the user already exists in Auth0.

2. **Given** an admin selects a language and creates the user, **When** that user logs into GEO, **Then** the whole interface (navigation, labels, wizard, dashboards, administration) renders in the selected language.

3. **Given** a user who already exists in Auth0, **When** the admin sets/changes the GEO language at creation, **Then** that language is **NOT propagated to Auth0** — the user's language in the other Onclusive apps is unchanged.

4. **Given** no language is chosen (or none is available from Auth0), **When** the user is created, **Then** the GEO language defaults to American English (en-US).

5. **(QA)** **Given** the QA team creates one test user per language (en-US, en-GB, fr-FR, es-ES) from administration, **When** each logs in, **Then** each sees the full platform in that language — **including en-GB and es-ES**, independently of Auth0/Middleware limitations.



1. New **nullable** column `users.ui_language_preference` (GEO locale); Flyway migration + MPD + `database_schema.md` updated. `users.language` unchanged (Auth0 cache, Pattern A intact). **[SUPERSÉDÉ par GEO-812]** — `ui_language_preference` supprimée, `users.language` devient GEO-owned full locale.

2. `/auth/me` resolves served language as `ui_language_preference ?? map(users.language) ?? "en-US"`. **[SUPERSÉDÉ par GEO-812]** — résolution = `user.getLanguage()` directement.

3. Provisioning write-logic: NOT_FOUND → both columns; EXISTS_AUTH0_ONLY → `ui_language_preference` only, no Auth0/Middleware push. **[SUPERSÉDÉ par GEO-812]** — write-path unifié vers `users.language` unique.

4. `ProvisioningWizard` dropdown: remove `disabled={foundOnAuth0}` (always editable); payload carries the chosen GEO locale. _(inchangé)_

5. en-GB / es-ES stored verbatim in `ui_language_preference`. **[SUPERSÉDÉ par GEO-812]** — stockage verbatim dans `users.language` directement.

6. Frontend read path accepts full GEO locale returned by `/auth/me` (en-GB passthrough). _(inchangé)_

7. Multi-tenancy/gating unchanged (provision = `SUPER_ADMIN`). _(inchangé)_

stories.title: [25.6] Send transactional emails in the recipient language
stories.userStory: As a GEO recipient (invited user, or report creator) whose language is known, I want the transactional emails I receive (welcome / set-password, analysis-ready) to be written in my own language, falling back to English when my language is not supported or not yet translated, so that I can read and act on them without translating them.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Given** a recipient has a language set, **When** they receive a transactional email from GEO, **Then** the email content is in their language.

2. **Given** a recipient has no supported language set, **When** they receive a transactional email from GEO, **Then** the email content falls back to English (en-US).


> ⚠️ **Content-block (QA, read before testing):** AC2 (English fallback) is **fully testable now**. **AC1 is content-blocked**: the mechanism is delivered, but the translated copy does not exist yet — the French/Spanish/British columns are **empty** for the 32 `email.*` keys in the source-of-truth CSV. Until the PM supplies the FR/ES copy, a `fr` recipient receives the email **in English** (per-key fallback) — that is the expected behaviour in this state, **not a bug**. Do not reject AC1 for "English email for a fr user" until the FR copy ships.  
⚠️ **V1 reachability:** only `en` (default) and `fr` are reachable via Auth0. `es` is not selectable until story 25.2 (backend currently normalizes `es → en`). `en-GB` is never auto-activated in V1. → Once FR copy ships, test AC1 with a recipient whose Auth0 language = `fr`.


1. A Spring `MessageSource` (emails basename) is configured and wired into the email `SpringTemplateEngine` (`EmailConfig.emailTemplateEngine()` via `setTemplateEngineMessageSource`); email templates render text from `messages_<locale>.properties` via Thymeleaf `#{...}` (no user-facing hardcoded text left in `welcome.html`, `analysis-ready.html`, `fragments/*`).

2. Email subjects (today concatenated in English in Java) are resolved via `messageSource.getMessage("email.<…>.subject", args, locale)` — subject and body follow the same locale.

3. Recipient language (`users.language`, heterogeneous format: short `en`/`fr` OR regional `fr-FR` per creation path — see 25.1 Q1) is resolved to a backend `Locale` **defensively** (mirror of the frontend `AUTH0_LANG_MAP`): `en|en-US|en-GB → en`, `fr|fr-FR → fr`, `es|es-ES → es`, any unknown → `en`.

4. The `EmailService` interface (`sendWelcomeEmail`, `sendAnalysisReadyEmail`) carries the recipient language, propagated by **all** call sites: `AdminUserService.provision`, `ReportStatusConsumer`, `ResendPasswordSetupService`, **and** `OpsController` (test endpoints). `NoOpEmailService` implements the new signature.

5. Mustache placeholders (`{{recipientFirstName}}`, `{{organisationName}}`, `{{year}}`) are converted to positional `{0}`/`{1}`… when emitting the `.properties`, and Java/Thymeleaf calls pass the args in the same order (otherwise interpolation fails silently).

6. A key missing from `messages_fr`/`messages_es` falls back to `messages.properties` (EN) — never blank, never `???key???` (`setUseCodeAsDefaultMessage(false)`, `setFallbackToSystemLocale(false)`, explicit EN default).

stories.title: [25.4] Translate the analysis wizard and onboarding
stories.userStory: As a GEO user with a supported language active, I want the analysis wizard and onboarding (its steps, fields, guidance, and screens) to appear in that language, so that I can configure and launch an analysis end-to-end in my own language.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Given** a supported language is active, **When** I use the analysis wizard, **Then** its steps, fields, and guidance appear in that language.

2. **Given** a supported language is active, **When** I go through onboarding, **Then** its screens appear in that language.


> ⚠️ **"Onboarding" = the 4-step analysis wizard (QA, read before testing).** Code investigation 2026-06-18: GEO has **no separate "onboarding" surface** (no `onboarding` namespace, no Onboarding/Welcome component). The PRD names the wizard itself a "4-step onboarding wizard". The `7-3-guided-tour` story (Epic 7) is a **separate, unshipped** feature — out of this Epic's scope. → **AC1 and AC2 target the same surface** (the wizard). See PM open question Q1.
> ⚠️ **Step 3 QUESTION TEXT is OUT of scope (QA, read before testing).** The questions shown in Step 3 ("Best {category}?", "Is {entity} a good {category} brand?", competitive questions with [Competitor N]) **do NOT follow the UI language**: they are backend-AI-adapted content (`POST /questions/adapt-batch`), keyed on the **analysed market language**. This matches the Epic's "Out of scope" (analysis-content translation). → **Do not fail the story** because a question's text is not in the UI language. Only the **wizard chrome** (labels, buttons, headers, guidance, info banners, states) follows the active language.
> ⚠️ **V1 reachability (QA, read before testing):** only en-US (default) and fr-FR are reachable via Auth0 in V1. **es-ES is not user-selectable until story 25.2** (backend currently normalizes `es → en`). **en-GB is never auto-activated in V1** (V2 dropdown only). → Test AC1/AC2 in **fr-FR**; es-ES/en-GB are covered by the technical AC (forced locale) until 25.2.
> ⚠️ **Known es-ES limitation (PM flag):** 3 wizard-scope keys (`wizard.category.quotaExceededByAi`, `wizard.topBar.ariaBack`, `wizard.topBar.newAnalysis`) are absent from the es-ES catalogue and fall back to English. This matches the OS-Team scoping decision (2026-06-18: es-ES EN-fallback acceptable, re-adding to the xlsx = product action) but is in literal tension with AC1. Do not reopen the ticket for these 3 keys until the product action ships.


1. With 25.1 merged (4 locales + fallback chain) and `fr-FR` active, every wizard surface (namespace `wizard.*`: steps, brand/market, category discovery, prompts, review, LLM toggles, modals, empty/loading states) renders via `t()` in French — zero residual hardcoded strings.

2. `pnpm lint:i18n` (eslint-plugin-i18next `no-literal-string`, mode `all`) exits 0 on `src/components/wizard/**`; any residual user-facing string is extracted to a `t()` key and added to all 4 locales.

3. A forced-locale render test (`i18next.changeLanguage("es-ES")` / `"en-GB"`) shows wizard surfaces render the requested locale for present keys and fall back cleanly to en-US for absent keys. Includes pluralized keys (`wizard.prompts.count_one`/`count_other`) checked at count 0/1/N per locale (i18next plural rules are locale-specific: fr-FR and es-ES differ from English).

4. The 3 es-ES wizard orphans stay in the explicit allow-list inherited from 25.1 (no new divergence introduced).

5. Any new key added to close a gap exists in all 4 locale files; fr-FR/es-ES values are supplied by the PM/source-of-truth (xlsx) — never invented.

stories.title: [25.5] Translate user administration and settings
stories.userStory: As a GEO administrator (or user) with a supported language active, I want the user administration screens (backoffice: users, organisations, provisioning, role/org modals, quotas) and my settings screen to appear in that language, so that account and configuration tasks are as clear as the rest of the app.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Given** a supported language is active, **When** I use user administration, **Then** those screens appear in that language.

2. **Given** a supported language is active, **When** I use my settings, **Then** those screens appear in that language.


> ⚠️ **V1 reachability (QA, read before testing):** only en-US (default) and fr-FR are reachable via Auth0 in V1. **es-ES is not user-selectable until story 25.2** (backend currently normalizes `es → en`). **en-GB is never auto-activated in V1** (V2 dropdown only). → Test AC1/AC2 in **fr-FR**; es-ES/en-GB are covered by the technical AC (forced locale) until 25.2.
> ⚠️ **Tighter reachability (specific to this story):** the administration screens are **gated to ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN** (`RequireBackofficeAccess`). The fr-FR functional test therefore requires an **admin/super-admin account whose Auth0 language is** `fr` — not just any fr user. This tightens the 25.2 soft-dep further: that admin's language is seeded by the same Auth0 path 25.2 fixes.
> ✅ **No orphans in this scope.** Unlike 25.3 (23 es-ES core orphans), the 25.5 scope (`backoffice.*` + `views.settings.*`) is **complete in all 4 languages** — verified by parity script 2026-06-18: `backoffice` = 198/198 keys across en-US/en-GB/fr-FR/es-ES, `views.settings` = 2/2. The 26 known es-ES orphans are all in `dashboard.*`/`views.*`/`wizard.*` (25.3/25.4), none here. → No AC1/AC2 tension, no orphan allow-list to manage.


1. With 25.1 merged (4 locales + fallback chain) and `fr-FR` active, every administration & settings surface (full `backoffice.*` namespace + `views.settings.*`) renders via `t()`/`<Trans>` in French — zero residual hardcoded strings.

2. `pnpm lint:i18n` (eslint-plugin-i18next `no-literal-string`, mode `all`, scope `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`) exits 0 on `src/backoffice/**` and `src/views/SettingsView.tsx`; any residual user-facing string is extracted to a `t()` key and added to all 4 locales (fr-FR/es-ES values supplied by the PM — never invented).

3. A forced-locale render test (`i18next.changeLanguage("es-ES")` / `"en-GB"`) shows representative backoffice/settings surfaces render the requested locale for present keys (all present in this scope) and fall back cleanly to en-US — verifying es-ES/en-GB independently of Auth0 inaccessibility in V1.

4. The parity test (25.1) keeps `backoffice.*` + `views.settings.*` at strict parity across the 4 locales (0 missing keys); this story introduces no new divergence or orphan.

5. Any new key added to close a gap exists in all 4 locale files; fr-FR/es-ES values are supplied by the PM/source-of-truth (xlsx) — never invented.

stories.title: [25.3] Translate the core interface
stories.userStory: As a GEO user with a supported language active, I want the core interface (navigation, buttons, labels, table headers, tooltips, empty states) to appear in that language and to stay in that language as I move between the views of an analysis, so that I can use GEO end-to-end in my own language.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Given** a supported language is active, **When** I navigate the app, **Then** navigation, buttons, labels, table headers, tooltips, and empty states all appear in that language.

2. **Given** a supported language is active, **When** I move between the different views of an analysis, **Then** the interface text stays in that language throughout.


> ⚠️ **V1 reachability (QA, read before testing):** only en-US (default) and fr-FR are reachable via Auth0 in V1. **es-ES is not user-selectable until story 25.2** (backend currently normalizes `es → en`). **en-GB is never auto-activated in V1** (V2 dropdown only). → Test AC1/AC2 in **fr-FR**; es-ES/en-GB are covered by the technical AC (forced locale) until 25.2.
> ⚠️ **Known es-ES limitation (PM flag):** 23 core-scope keys (`dashboard.sov.*`, `dashboard.reportError.*`, `views.addCategory.*`, `views.upsell.seeItInAction*`) are absent from the es-ES catalogue and fall back to English. This matches the OS-Team scoping decision (2026-06-18: es-ES EN-fallback acceptable, re-adding to the xlsx = product action) but is in literal tension with AC1. Do not reopen the ticket for these 23 keys until the product action ships.

stories.title: [25.2] Seed the language from Auth0 at user creation
stories.userStory: As an org administrator provisioning a new GEO user, I want the new user's interface language to be pre-selected from their Auth0 language (and editable among the supported languages, defaulting to English when none is usable), so that users land in GEO already in the right language without me re-keying it, while GEO stays a write-through cache of Auth0 (no GEO-local override in V1).
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Given** a language is set for a user in Auth0, **When** that user is added to GEO via the provisioning wizard, **Then** that language is retrieved and pre-selected as the default in the language choice on the user creation step.

2. **Given** the Auth0 language is pre-selected during user creation, **When** I am adding the user, **Then** I can change it to any of the four supported languages (American English, British English, French, Spanish) before confirming.

3. **Given** no usable language is available from Auth0 (absent or unsupported), **When** the user is added, **Then** the language choice defaults to English (en-US).

4. **Given** an existing Auth0 user whose language is French or Spanish, **When** I look them up in the wizard (step 1 → step 2), **Then** the pre-selected value reflects their actual Auth0 language (French → French, Spanish → Spanish) — not a silent fallback to English.



1. `AdminUserService.VALID_LANGUAGES` accepts the V1 short codes `{en, fr, es}` (adds `es`); any value outside → `ValidationException("INVALID_LANGUAGE: supported values are en, fr, es")`.

2. `MiddlewareClient.MIDDLEWARE_LANG_CODES` maps `en → "en"`, `fr → "fr-FR"`, `es → "es"` (exact values from the case-sensitive Middleware allowlist `zh-CN,fr-FR,es,it,de,en`).

3. The Auth0 read path (`searchAuth0ByEmail`) accepts both short and regional codes produced by our own write path and returns the GEO short code (`fr-FR|fr → fr`, `es-ES|es → es`, `en-US|en-GB|en → en`); anything else → `null`. (Fixes the existing write/read asymmetry — required for AC1/AC4.)

4. The provisioning wizard dropdown (`prov-lang`) offers the four languages; `ProvisionUserPayload.language` covers the emitted codes (`en | fr | es`); `data-testid="prov-lang"` preserved.

5. The seed contract stays **Pattern A** (write-through Auth0 cache): `users.language` stores the resolved short code (`en`/`fr`/`es`). **[SUPERSÉDÉ par GEO-812]** — `users.language` sera une locale GEO complète (`en-US|en-GB|fr-FR|es-ES`). Voir GEO-812.

6. Multi-tenancy: `POST /api/v1/admin/users/provision` and `GET /api/v1/admin/users/search/auth0` stay `@PreAuthorize`-gated at backoffice level.

stories.title: [25.1] Foundation — i18n 4-locale extension + fallback chain
stories.userStory: As the GEO frontend platform, I want the i18n layer to support the four languages (en-US, en-GB, fr-FR, es-ES) with a deterministic fallback chain sourced from the user's Auth0 language, so that every other V1 story builds on an accurate locale infrastructure and any not-yet-translated text degrades gracefully to English.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Given** a supported language is active, **When** a screen renders text not yet translated in that language, **Then** the text falls back to English (en-US) — never a blank or a missing-key marker (US 1.7).

2. **Given** some text on a screen falls back to English, **When** the screen renders, **Then** the rest of the screen stays in the active language (per-key fallback, not per-screen).

3. **Given** a user whose Auth0 language is one of the four supported, **When** the app loads after auth resolves, **Then** the interface renders in that language.

4. **Given** a user with no usable Auth0 language (absent or unsupported), **When** the app loads, **Then** the interface renders in American English (en-US).



1. `i18n.ts` registers the four locale resources and a fallback chain: en-GB → en-US, fr-FR → en-US, es-ES → en-US, default en-US.

2. `useSyncI18nLanguage.tsx` — `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` holds the four codes; `AUTH0_LANG_MAP` is defensive (accepts short + regional codes); unknown → en-US.

3. `types.ts` `Language` enum reflects the four locales; `TranslationKeys` unchanged.

4. `useTranslations.ts` `currentLanguage` type covers the four codes.

5. Catalogue integrity test extended to 4-locale key parity (es-ES orphan allow-list); `fr = en` invariant relaxed.

stories.title: Retrieve UP existing terminology inventory by language
stories.userStory: As a product manager preparing GEO for multi-language support, I want a per-language inventory of the terminology already in use across UP (Universe Platform), so that the GEO translations can reuse existing UP wording for shared concepts instead of inventing new translations - keeping the platform consistent for users who already use other UP modules.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
- Given the inventory is delivered, When I open the file, Then I see one column per target language (French, British English, American English, Spanish) populated with the existing UP wording for each term.
- Given a UP term covers a concept also used in GEO, When the file is reviewed, Then the term is flagged as GEO-relevant so it can be picked up by the GEO English source-of-truth file.
- Given multiple UP variations exist for the same concept across modules, When the inventory is captured, Then the variations are listed together so reviewers can pick the canonical one.
- Given the file exists, When the GEO localization implementation starts, Then the GEO English-and-translations file reuses the UP wording for every term that overlaps.

stories.title: Prepare English source-of-truth file for all user-facing messages and gather translations
stories.userStory: As a product owner preparing the platform for multi-language support (French, British English, American English, Spanish), I want a single English source-of-truth file that lists every user-facing message in the app together with its surface and context, so that we can review and validate the English wording in one pass, then attach the translations for each target language alongside it.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
- Given the inventory is complete, When I read the document, Then every user-facing string in the platform is listed once with surface, trigger, and current English wording.
- Given a string appears in multiple surfaces, When the inventory is reviewed, Then it is noted in each context (so reviewers can spot inconsistencies in usage).
- Given dynamic strings (e.g., "X reports generated"), When listed, Then the template is captured with placeholders rather than a rendered example.
- Given the English column has been validated, When translations are added, Then there is one column per target language (French, British English, American English, Spanish) and each entry is filled in.
- Given UP already uses a term for a given concept, When the translation is filled in, Then the existing UP wording is reused for consistency (rather than inventing a new translation).
- Given the file exists, When localization implementation starts, Then this document becomes the single source of truth used to populate the translation keys across the platform.
